sourcePdf.pageConvention: PDF page number = printed page + 1; image filenames use 1-based PDF page numbers.

scope: Five-map static source relationship audit: main floor plans, relative elevations, stairs and inter-level links, room-group footprints, entry, foundation and external placement intent, materials and relevant water relationships.
outcome: All 31 levels received the declared static structure source comparison. None is claimed to have passed the complete all-map logic/runtime audit merely because it was reviewed. Castle is explicitly partial and has source contradictions as well as confirmed implementation gaps.
method: Read source OCR spatial passages and inspected all primary map panels at local full-page resolution.
Compared the exact committed scene JSON, authoring generators and atlas; generated CPU polygon diagrams for every level.
Inventoried all 370 room polygons and all 82 links; measured explicit dimensions and relationships identified in the report.
Kept exact source dimensions, approximate descriptions and internally conflicting source numbers in distinct categories.
Kept source images local outside Git and used original wording for relationship summaries.

relations.sourceRelationship: The entrance stair first reaches a landing 30 ft up, then the audience floor another 20 ft up. The next main floor is 40 ft higher. The exterior roof is described at 130 ft above the court.
relations.baselineObservation: Datums 0,30,50,90,130 preserve these relationships. The chapel balcony at +50 and chapel room ceiling 90 also agree.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: K12 is a 30-ft octagon; K19 measures 40 by 20 ft; K20 begins 60 ft across; K24 is described as 40 by 20 ft.
relations.baselineObservation: K12 and K19 bounds agree. K20 is 35 by 35 ft, while K24 is 35 by 20 ft. These are explicit dimension differences, not a percentage-based tolerance test.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The concealed ladder in K34 climbs 20 ft into K20.
relations.baselineObservation: lk-k34-ladder starts on court +50 and lands on ground 0, a 50-ft descent. Its endpoint displacement is also about 43.5 ft in plan. The source requires an upward route.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The floor plan labels a 30-ft stair from K24 to K34, then the 20-ft hidden ladder reaches K20 on the +50 floor.
relations.baselineObservation: K34 is grouped into the +50 court level, and lk-k24 rises 50 ft. This grouping loses the lower K34 landing indicated by the map.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The elevator rises 170 ft overall, passing landings 90 and 130 ft above its base.
relations.baselineObservation: The floor datums -40,+50,+90,+130 match 90/130/170 ft. The link preserves the total rise, although its plan endpoints differ and exact shaft alignment needs correction.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The elevator and counterweight move in one vertical shaft.
relations.baselineObservation: lk-elevator changes plan position from [180,195] to [170,204], a 13.4536-ft horizontal shift. The source does not describe a sloping or laterally transferring elevator.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: K79 has two 45-degree flights, running 40 and 30 ft horizontally. The printed basement plate also labels 70-ft ascents at K79 and K83.
relations.baselineObservation: The corresponding level change is only 40 ft (-80 to -40). The K79 lower prop rises 40 ft and its upper prop 0.1 ft. K83 is likewise reduced to that 40-ft level difference.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The flooded cell corridors are 2 ft below K73. K77 overlooks K76 from 10 ft higher. K80 gains 20 ft. The three outer tomb approaches descend below the catacomb floor.
relations.baselineObservation: All those rooms share one -80-ft floor. K77 chairs are at local y=0; same-level links for K80/K85/K86/K87 supply no floor elevation change. K80 prop rise is 10 ft instead of the described 20 ft. The 2-ft cell step is not encoded in room floors.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: K88 windows are reached by descending 110 ft from K6 and moving back beneath that overlook.
relations.baselineObservation: K6 floor is 0 and K88 is -80, so the authored levels differ by only 80 ft. Their polygons and window object do not restore the 110-ft vertical relationship.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The high-tower sources disagree: staircase text gives 300 ft, shaft text gives 390 ft, the peak narrative gives 450 ft, and map 10 labels a 380-ft drop. Other map captions also differ from adjacent text.
relations.baselineObservation: The baseline chooses high-peak +300 and dungeon -80, yielding 380 ft, so it follows the map-10 drop but cannot satisfy all narrative numbers. It is not sound to label one of those competing numbers uniquely authoritative without a documented convention.
relations.disposition: Choose and document a consistent castle datum convention before reauthoring the high tower; preserve the explicit source conflict in the decision.

relations.sourceRelationship: Map 7 labels 20-ft changes to maps 6 and 8; map 8 places its K20 landing 190 ft above the main floor. The roof narrative gives 130 ft, while K57 prose gives an 80-ft drop to that roof and K58 gives 60 ft.
relations.baselineObservation: The baseline uses +130,+150,+190: 20 then 40 ft. The map-7 to map-8 increment is therefore not preserved. Some underlying source numbers conflict, so a coherent split between roof and tower floors is needed.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: K57 is explicitly 60 ft in diameter; K60a is enclosed by a 20-ft-diameter ring.
relations.baselineObservation: K57 polygon spans 40 ft and K60a spans 35 ft. The two tower sizes are both inconsistent with those explicit source dimensions.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The map has a 50-ft ascent from the +190 heart landing to K60. K60 has a 9-ft ceiling and roof access. K60a narrative places the courtyard 260 ft below.
relations.baselineObservation: K60 at +240 matches the map. K60a at +250 differs from the explicit 260-ft courtyard drop; the 9-ft ladder plus floor thickness is the apparent authoring assumption, not an explanation recorded in the source.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: K41 is an octagonal room containing a square 20-ft tower.
relations.baselineObservation: The room polygon is a 25-by-20-ft rectangle. The prop remains a 20-by-20-ft tower, so the source room shape is lost.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The numbered catacomb crypts are hollow chambers with separate access and some deeper spaces; crypt 14 leads 40 ft down into a vault, and two other crypts contain deep pits.
relations.baselineObservation: The scene has 40 solid column props and labels, no separate crypt interiors, no lower vault level, and no link to the crypt-14 vault. The scene is already marked partial=true; the source review confirms that limitation rather than treating the labels as complete spatial coverage.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The catacomb extent is described approximately as 110 by 180 ft.
relations.baselineObservation: K84 bounds are 140 by 190 ft. Record the difference; no invented percentage threshold converts this approximate textual size into a strict failure.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The western drawbridge immediately connects the castle entrance at J to the castle court. The eastern overlook and cliff face belong to the same castle.
relations.baselineObservation: The source plan confirms immediate adjacency. Baseline atlas gives J and K independent root placements; the prior exact-baseline probe measured 4598.4526 ft between their root pins and a 583.815-ft datum difference. Removing distant stand-ins alone cannot establish entrance continuity.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: Four house storeys have successive ceiling heights 10,12,8,13 ft; the two exterior balconies are on the third storey. The printed floor plans use 5-ft squares.
relations.baselineObservation: House datums 0,10,22,30 and ceilings 10,12,8,13 match. The 30-by-55-ft plan and front/back third-floor balconies are present. North is -x, matching the printed compass.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The main stair joins the first three floors; the small service shaft joins kitchen, servants and main bedroom. A concealed attic stair is reachable from the third-floor hall and bedroom.
relations.baselineObservation: Main-stair and service-shaft endpoints use a common x/z on all three floors. One attic stair link is present with the source doors in the adjacent third-floor rooms. CPU plan comparison finds the intended room-group adjacency.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The narrow secret shaft descends 50 ft from attic room 21 to dungeon access 22, passing through the house.
relations.baselineObservation: The vertical difference +30 to -20 is correct, but the link moves from [2.5,17.5] to [59.5,20.5], or 57.0789 ft sideways. Dungeon and house plans were not registered onto the same shaft.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The dungeon stair reaches a trapdoor directly beneath the den floor.
relations.baselineObservation: lk-trapdoor connects [87.5,56.5] in the dungeon to [27.5,52.5] in the house: 60.1332 ft sideways. The source does not provide a lateral passage above the landing to explain that separation.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The 20-ft stair at area 30 is the continuous descent to area 35.
relations.baselineObservation: Its link endpoints are 66.5676 ft apart in plan ([45,75] and [7.5,20]); both stair props use rise=0.1 even though level datums differ by 10 ft. The separate printed panels have not been registered into one physical stair.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The approach to the portcullis slopes down at 20 degrees; water is 2 ft deep, while ledges and the central dais stand 5 ft above the basin floor. The chamber is 40 ft square and 16 ft high.
relations.baselineObservation: The room plan and 5-ft ledge/dais props and 16-ft room ceiling agree. Areas 35,37,38 share one flat -30-ft level; no slope geometry is authored for the 20-degree approach. Water depth exists in DM text, but the floor uses a shallow-water material rather than a measured basin/water datum pair.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The house feature summary specifies timber floors throughout the interior.
relations.baselineObservation: Several indoor rooms use flagstone, including kitchen/pantry and bathroom/secret-stair spaces. This is a material disagreement; the stone entrance portico is exterior and is not counted as an interior contradiction.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The house is in the village and its earthen dungeon may extend beyond the house walls. Underground extent alone does not imply exposed outdoor rooms.
relations.baselineObservation: The source house plan is 30 by 55 ft, while its parent E7 marker is about 21.2 ft square. The 2.09x inventory warning is a nested-placement conflict, not evidence to shrink the canonical room plan. Basement registration and terrain masking remain separate issues.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The entrance descends 10 ft from the front ledge, then the balcony stairs descend 30 ft to the main hall. The library is likewise 30 ft above its lower vault.
relations.baselineObservation: Datums +40,+30,0 preserve these changes. The main stairs and library spiral encode 30-ft rises. Both plans share the four columns, large southern stairs, and temple axis.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The temple is cut into the mountain. The snowy approach reaches its southern facade, and the hall/vault plans extend north behind it. The western fissure is a second entrance.
relations.baselineObservation: The facade-only outdoor bounds exclude most of the underground plans, which is consistent with source intent. It is not a source defect simply that rooms lie outside the apron footprint. Section navigation must expose those rooms without asserting that the entire temple is an open-air pit.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The facade is 50 ft high with six 20-ft statues and a 20-ft-high entry. The paired upper halls are each 20 by 70 ft; the entrance guard rooms/barracks are 20-ft squares.
relations.baselineObservation: Facade and statue dimensions, room bounds and paired hallway lengths agree. Snow outside, black stone floors and amber wall/door treatment agree with the material intent.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The lecture-hall stairs descend 20 ft toward the lectern, with seating following that internal change in height.
relations.baselineObservation: X9 remains on one +30-ft floor. The two step props have rise=2; bench positions use local y=1.6,0.8,0; lectern y=0. The intended 20-ft internal descent has been reduced by a factor of ten.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The X6 hole and X33a ceiling shaft are aligned vertically, with a 20-ft shaft and a final 10-ft drop to the vault floor.
relations.baselineObservation: X-shaft uses [205,235] at both endpoints, separated by 30 ft. X33a room ceiling is 10 ft. The combined geometry is consistent with the source relationship.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: X14 and X21 connect upper and lower halls by three flights; X26 can open over the northwest of X39; X5b connects the main hall to the library; X41 connects the treasury and northern vault.
relations.baselineObservation: All named routes are represented. X26 bounds [80,90,90,100] project into X39. X14 and X21 links span the correct 30-ft level difference. The northern fissure is an abstracted 10-by-10-ft polygon rather than two explicit narrow passages.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The southern catacombs are continuous passages around solid internal blocks, with side chambers joined by necks.
relations.baselineObservation: X31, X31a and X31b are authored as self-intersecting polygons. The intended loops are recognizable on the source plan, but their computational boundary representation is invalid and cannot safely be treated as a verified interior footprint.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The ruin uses stone, amber and rock; it has no river or bridge crossing inside these plans. The small castle model in X20 is an interior object, not a second full castle.
relations.baselineObservation: Water flow is not applicable to the interior structure. The castle model is intentionally retained. Any regional mountain seam, scene excavation, or proxy overlap requires the owner’s rendered checks; source intent alone cannot certify those transitions.
relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The two stair flights from the northern gate rise 10 ft to the mansion doors. The cemetery also reaches the chapel by an exterior stair.

relations.sourceRelationship: The south wing is collapsed, exposing three floor edges, while the open foyer and chapel remain vertically connected. The roof opening lies above Q33.

relations.sourceRelationship: The roof hole opens directly over Q33, whose floor is 20 ft below.

relations.sourceRelationship: The upper landing reaches the beacon room by timber stairs; the room has a 30-ft pitched roof. The excerpt does not assign an exact additional rise from the 80-ft landing.

relations.disposition: Record for the implementation owner; this audit makes no application changes.

relations.sourceRelationship: The mansion occupies elevated ground; the drive and dragon statue are west, the cemetery northeast, and the beacon rises over the eastern chapel apse. Ruined stone, timber floors, roof tiles and small rainwater pools define the visible materials.
